---
title: "Durable Picos with celld"
subtitle: "From Hello, Pico! to a persistent, addressable, hibernating actor"
---

## The architectural lesson

```
A Pico is not a container.
A Pico is not a process.
A Pico is not a Kubernetes Pod.
A Pico is not a Durable Object.
A Pico is not celld.

              Pico
                │
                ▼
        engineering entity
                │
                ▼
           Runtime SPI
          ╱      │      ╲
         ╱       │       ╲
     Native    celld     future
                │
                ▼
          Durable Actor
```

**Pico is the Open Engineering abstraction. celld is one possible runtime implementation.**

## The central experiment

```
POST hello  →  event_count = 1
POST hello  →  event_count = 2
# restart runtime
POST hello  →  event_count = 3
```

State belongs to the Pico, not to the process that last executed it.

## What you will build

| Artifact | Role |
|----------|------|
| `HelloPico` | Domain behaviour (runtime-independent) |
| `PicoRuntime` SPI | Abstract deploy / invoke / inspect / … |
| `NativeRuntime` | Volatile in-process baseline |
| `DurableRuntime` | SQLite-backed durable adapter (celld-shaped) |
| Contract tests | Same suite passes on both runtimes |

## Learning path

```
Hello, Pico!
     │
     ▼
State vs process
     │
     ▼
Actor model
     │
     ▼
Pico Runtime SPI
     │
     ▼
Durable state + restart recovery
     │
     ├─ multiple identities
     ├─ alarms / hibernation
     ├─ containers / Minikube
     └─ Crossplane / Manifold (reuse Academy material)
```

## Runtime package

Working code lives in `runtime/`:

```bash
cd runtime
PYTHONPATH=src python -m pytest tests -q
# 18 passed
```

## Principle

> Prefer a semantic runtime request (`class: durable`) over hard-coding an implementation (`implementation: celld`).
